regions.text: 若いたものであらう。これらは假說約偶然すなはち理由性因果性目前性の否定としての偶然性の聽覺象徴としては極めて適切なものである。

quote.translation: As auditory symbols of contingency in the sense of hypothetical contingency, that is, of contingency as the negation of groundedness, causality and purposiveness, these words are extremely apt.

regions.text: 序に偶然性の視覺的象徴を擧げようとするならば、ラメトリイにつて「日々に生え出る茸のやうに】（semblablcaceschampignonsquiparaissentd'unjouralautre）とい^LaMetrie,L'Fommemachine,Puris1365p.96）こも出來る。

quote.translation: If we wished, incidentally, to give a visual symbol of contingency, we could say with La Mettrie "like those mushrooms that spring up from one day to the next" (semblable à ces champignons qui paraissent d'un jour à l'autre) (La Mettrie, L'Homme machine, Paris, 1865, p. 98).

regions.text: 成瀬無極氏の偶然間答には「線の下から飛び出した蛙』（偶然開答区三三質図三六百）といふ醫喩が用ひてある。

quote.translation: In Naruse Mukyoku's "Dialogue on Chance" the metaphor of "a frog that jumped out from under the veranda" is used (Dialogue on Chance, pp. 433, 436).

regions.text: ギリシアでは偶然すなはちテュク（さべ）、を女神として祭つた場合その持物としては樽々する「球」とか「車輪とか、または閣々たる羽」を持たせた。

quote.translation: In Greece, when chance, that is, Tychē (τύχη), was worshipped as a goddess, she was given as her attributes a rolling "ball" or "wheel", or a fluttering "feather".

regions.text: 様相前範職の一つとしての偶然性の頑覺的象徴は記號的論理學にとつても全然開心を映くべき事柄ではない。

quote.translation: The visual symbol of contingency as one of the modal categories is not, moreover, a matter that symbolic logic can regard with complete indifference.

regions.text: 後に偶然性の記跳として互を選んだのは、「獨立なる二元の避遍」をしての偶然性の象徴化にほかならない（一九六百照。

quote.translation: When I later choose )( as the sign of contingency, this is nothing other than a symbolisation of contingency as "the Encounter of two independent elements" (獨立なる二元の邂逅) (see p. 196).

Lewis, A Survey of Symbolic Logic, 1918, p. 293, 312) (see p. 193) calls the property common to apodicticity (see p. 198), that is, to impossibility (~) and necessity (~-), "strict implication" (Strict Implication), and the property common to assertoricity, that is, to truth ( ) and falsity (-), "material implication" (Material Implication); and he calls the property common to problematicity, that is, to possibility (-~) and contingency (-~-), "consistency" (Consistency).
